1.text: Thee. The just may offend: but the wicked relapse continually.

2.text: Hold. Gr. "bite," (C.) in the same sense. M. --- Serpents sting in secret: so all sins inveigle the soul. W.

3.text: Lion. Yet only those are hurt, who consent to sin. The devil may go round about, (1 Pet. v. 8.) and tempt; (C.) he cannot bit, except a man willingly expose himself, and come near. v. 2.

4.text: Remedy. In man. H. --- Only the sovereign physician can cure it. C.

5.text: Riches. As they make enemies arise. Gr. subjoins, "so the house of the proud shall be made desolate." H. --- Roboam lost ten tribes by an insolent answer, and the Tarquins were expelled for their pride.

6.text: Speedily. God is the protector of the poor. Ps. x. 5.

7.text: Sinner. He rejects all medicines. How shall he be cured? C. --- They who fear God, will examine their actions when they are warned. W.

8.text: By him. And to avoid his reproaches. Gr. "knoweth when he is ruined." H. --- He is more reserved, and escapes the dangers of talkativeness.

9.text: Winter. This season is unfit for building; so the man who borrows, may be forced to pay again (C.) before it is convenient for him. H. --- Injustice will bring on ruin. Jer. xxiii. 13. Some Gr. copies have, "stones for a heap over his tomb," as Achan and Absalom were treated. Reputation, or goods ill-acquired, will not continue long. W.

10.text: Fire. All their grandeur will end in smoke. H. --- Mal. iv. 1. Matt. xiii. 30.

11.text: Stones. It is broad and easy. Matt. vii.

12.text: Thereof. Practice makes perfect. A painter may produce a better piece by this means, than one who is more acquainted with theory, (C.) and neglects it. H.

15.text: Bitterness. True wisdom promotes the general good.

16.text: Of life. Which never fails. Jo. iv. 14. and vii. 38.

20.text: Church. Or assembly, Job xxix. 11. 21. C. --- All good people dislike senseless talk, and approve of what is edifying. W.

21.text: Fool. All is in confusion, like a heap of ruins.

23.text: Low. A smiling countenance is commendable, but loud laughter is to be avoided. Clem. Pæd. ii. 5. --- It causes too great a change, (Plato, Rep. 3.) and is a mark of folly. Eccle. vii. 5. S. Aug. c. Acad. ii. 2.

25.text: House. And meddles with the concerns of others. C. --- Of the mighty, is not in Gr. The wise will not easily receive invitations. H.

29.text: Heart. Understanding. H. --- The wise speak with reflection. Prov. xvi. 23.

30.text: While the ungodly, &c. He condemneth and curseth himself; inasmuch as by sin he takes part with the devil, and is, as it were, his member and subject. Ch. --- In vain does he lay the blame of his sins on the devil. v. 3. C. --- He condemns himself by imitating the wicked. Lu. xix. W.

31.text: By all. Gr. "in the neighbourhood." The rest is omitted. H.
